title: Cambyses of Persia conquers Egypt
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024)). Sorted by the CFAH anchor point cited below (added by the Herodotus import); the Generations dates are display only.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 3: Anchor Points of Ancient History," ARJ 16 (2023): 131–154, section "AP-8: Battle of Pelusium: 525 B.C.—Persian Conquest of Egypt"
chronologies.note: CFAH-3: "The conquest of Egypt at the Battle of Pelusium in May of 525 B.C. occurred in the fifth year of Cambyses’ reign. Subtracting five and thirty years from the Era of Cyrus in 560 B.C. yields 525 B.C." (CFAH counts Cyrus 30 years; Herodotus 1.214 gives 29.)

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 16 "The Fall of Egypt by God's Decree–The Middle and Late Empires of Egypt", PDF p. 408 (printed p. 394)

chronologies.date: “The above-mentioned Amasis was the Egyptian king against whom Cambyses, son of Cyrus, made his expedition”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.1 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 175 (PDF p. 177)

chronologies.date: “he had died after ruling Egypt forty and four years”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.10 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 178 (PDF p. 180)
chronologies.note: Amasis died before Cambyses arrived; Psammenitus his son was king. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 525 BC (CFAH AP-8) + ½ year (Psammenitus) + 44 = about 570/569 BC for Amasis's accession.

chronologies.date: “whose whole reign had been but six months”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.14 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 180 (PDF p. 182)
chronologies.note: Ten days after the fall of Memphis. Consistent with CFAH AP-8 (525 BC), Generations 525 BC.
